messages:
alex: Heads-up — hit a crash in the async Python client when the server returns an error body that's raw non-UTF8 bytes. Repro included below, happens in our error parsing path (we try to .decode() and blow up).

alex: repro (aiohttp):
```py
import aiohttp, asyncio

async def hit():
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
        async with s.post('https://example.test/bad', data=b'\xff\xfe\x00\x01') as r:
            text = await r.text()  # raises UnicodeDecodeError for non-utf8
            print(r.status, text)

asyncio.run(hit())
```

alex: stack (trimmed):
```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 0: invalid start byte
  File "redwood_client/_errors.py", line 87, in _parse_error
    body = response.content.decode()
```

mina: Ugh. I remember a similar flake when an internal service sent latin1 blobs for debugging. We should never raise while constructing the exception.

sam: Agreed. Proposal: keep raw bytes on the exception (raw_body: bytes) and expose .text doing decode(errors='replace'). That way consumers can still inspect raw. Also make the typed exception shape explicit: HTTPError(status: int, message: Optional[str], raw_body: bytes, request_id: Optional[str]).

ivy: +1 on typed dataclass-like exceptions. Also add a helper `error_body_as_str(response)` that centralizes error decoding rules (try utf-8, fall back to latin1, finally errors='replace').

alex: I'll open a tiny PR with tests and a sampleapp reproducer. Quick workaround for folks: wrap client call in try/except UnicodeDecodeError and log response.content. But that's gross. :grimacing:

sam: Small add: ensure async path doesn't call any .text property synchronously — await .text() or use response.content.read() then handle bytes. The bug is more common in our async code path because we assume `.content` is str.

mina: Can we also ensure exception keeps original headers so we can surf for content-type? If server set `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=latin1` we should decode properly.

alex: Good point — I'll include headers in the exception metadata (as raw list/tuple). Also will add unit tests that simulate different content-types and byte sequences.

ci-bot: CI triggered: https://ci.redwood/12345 — running tests for PR #2046.

mina: Please add a short sampleapp in examples/ that shows how to reproduce locally (dockerized simple flask returning bytes). Makes it easier for platform folks to debug.

alex: Will do. PR link when ready; assigning @mina for review. Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
